items.title: Unhealthy API readings recorded in 10 areas nationwide as of 4pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 10 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today, according to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS). In Sarawak, seven areas recorded unhealthy levels: Serian (178), Samarahan (177), Kuching (174), Sri Aman (162), Sarikei (157), Mukah (152), and Sibu (151). Meanwhile, 56 areas recorded moderate API levels, while two areas recorded good air quality.

items.title: Malaysia needs more engineers to keep pace with data centre boom
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to accelerate the production of engineers and highly skilled technicians to keep pace with the rapid growth of data centre investments in the country. Data centre chief consultant Lee Cheng Pay said while Malaysia currently has sufficient local talent to support the industry, the pace of new investments meant more engineers would be needed over the next four to five years. Lee said the influx of foreign engineers during the early stages of Malaysia's data centre development had also helped local engineers gain exposure to advanced technologies and industry practices.

items.title: Civil servant held over alleged RM19k bribes in Pahang
items.summary: KUANTAN: A civil servant has been arrested for allegedly accepting about RM19,000 in bribes to help companies and individuals secure tenders and contracts at a government agency in Pahang. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) obtained a five-day remand order until Aug 19 to facilitate investigations. An MACC source said the suspect was arrested after she went to the Temerloh MACC office to give her statement at 6.45pm yesterday.

items.title: Former Nepal premier Deuba returns home, faces graft probe
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Former Nepal prime minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, facing arrest for alleged corruption, returned home Thursday, six months after leaving for medical treatment abroad. In April, police issued an arrest warrant for Deuba over money laundering charges, making him the latest high-profile figure targeted under the new government of Prime Minister Balendra Shah. Authorities had also issued a warrant for Deuba's wife, former foreign minister Arzu Rana Deuba.

items.title: Fake names, dead phone numbers: How Customs unravelled a RM1m cannabis export plot at KLIA
items.summary: SEPANG, Aug 13 — The use of fake sender and recipient addresses, as well as unreachable telephone numbers, was uncovered in an attempt to export 12.675 kilogrammes (kg) of cannabis buds worth RM1.014 million via courier service to a European country last July. Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Customs director Aspalila Ag Tuah said the addresses stated on the four packages containing the drugs were identified as being in the Klang Valley, but investigations found that the information was false. On July 13, the Enforcement Division operations team seized four packages suspected of containing cannabis buds at a mail and courier centre branch.

items.title: Erosion threatens Tanjung Asam beach in Penang
items.summary: The beach, once known for its clean sand, has gradually been eroded by strong waves, while sections of the shoreline defence have collapsed. Fisherman Aim Chin Seng, 35, said the damage had been noticeable for several years but had worsened recently. He said the impact was clearly visible, with the stone embankment built as a wave barrier badly damaged by strong waves.

items.title: Ong Kian Ming hopes DAP delegates will vote for party to quit cabinet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A former DAP member of parliament has expressed hope that delegates at this Sunday's congress will vote for the party to quit Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's cabinet. However, the former Bangi MP said there was only one compelling reason for DAP to leave the cabinet — to pressure Anwar into delivering political reforms before the next general election. He said that if delegates voted for DAP leaders to remain in the cabinet despite these developments, Anwar could interpret it as a signal that DAP would continue supporting the government until the end of the parliamentary term, regardless of whether substantive reforms were introduced.

items.title: Cough and flu remedies flying off the shelves as Sibu’s haze refuses to clear
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 13 — The haze situation in Sibu remained at an unhealthy level today, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) recorded at 152 as of 4pm, unchanged from Wednesday. Local pharmacist Juliana Ting said demand for cough and flu medication had surged amid the hazy conditions, although there had been no significant increase in demand for eye medication or inhalers. “Cough, sore throat, flu, headache and fever are among the common health problems experienced by people during unhealthy haze conditions,” she said when met.

items.title: Italy's Meloni has a youth problem as election approaches
items.summary: ITALIAN Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government is increasingly unpopular among young voters, opinion polls show, a trend that could prove costly ahead of a national election due next year. At the peak of Meloni's popularity in 2023, Youtrend polling showed her party alone attracted roughly the same support among young people as the whole ruling coalition does now. The sharpest party divides showed support for Meloni's FDI at 15 per cent among 18- to 29-year-old men and just 4.2 per cent among women, while 5-Star was backed by 18 per cent of women under 30, and just 5.1 per cent of men.

items.title: Govt to reassess Sosma, refugee policies against current needs, says home minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — The direction of the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Sosma) and the issue of refugees require in-depth scrutiny to ensure that policies and measures remain relevant to current developments and national needs, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. Saifuddin Nasution, who chaired a discussion on the two issues this morning, said neither should be viewed from a single perspective, but instead assessed by taking into account recent developments, challenges on the ground and possible approaches for the future. Sosma, which was introduced in 2012, provides authorities with special measures to address security offences and replaced the Internal Security Act 1960 (ISA), which was subsequently repealed.

items.title: As air quality turns unhealthy at Minden, Penang exco urges public to limit outdoor activities
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 13 — Air quality in parts of Penang reached unhealthy levels today, with the Minden monitoring station recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 107 at noon before improving later in the afternoon. Penang housing and environment committee chairman Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo said the Minden station recorded an API reading of 107 at noon, followed by 103 at 1pm, both within the unhealthy category. Sundarajoo said Penang had four automated air quality monitoring stations operated by the Department of Environment (DoE), located in Seberang Jaya, Seberang Perai, Minden and Balik Pulau.

items.title: Two directors in Perak plead not guilty to faking Socso job incentive claims
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 13 — Two company directors pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court today to charges of submitting false documents under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 incentive claims two years ago. Leong, a director of MS Solution Management Services and MN Tree Resources, is accused of submitting a false Employee Confirmation Form to a Perkeso officer with intent to deceive. Phun, a director of CKIN Management Services and Diligent Cleaning Solution, faces similar charges for submitting false forms to two Perkeso officers with the same intent.

items.title: Penang air quality hit unhealthy levels before slight improvement
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Air quality in Penang ranged from moderate to unhealthy today, with the Minden monitoring station recording an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading. The Penang government said API readings across the state ranged from 60 to 107 between Aug 10 and 13 as regional hotspots increased. Penang has four automatic air quality monitoring stations in Seberang Jaya, Seberang Prai, Minden and Balik Pulau.

items.title: MACC’s KWAP eFishery probe is almost done at home — now it’s waiting on overseas banks
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has so far found no evidence of criminal wrongdoing involving corruption or misappropriation in the Retirement Fund Incorporated’s (KWAP) RM163.4 million investment in Indonesian aquaculture firm eFishery. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said, however, that the full findings would only be available after investigators obtained financial information and documents from overseas banks, including those in Singapore and Indonesia. Abd Halim said investigators were also working to obtain statements from identified witnesses who were currently overseas.

items.title: Gaza cancer patients face rising death rate amid Israeli curbs
items.summary: CAIRO: Gaza cancer patients are dying at two to three times the pace they did before the start of the war in the territory, as Israel blocks many from travelling for treatment after destroying the only local specialised facility, Gaza doctors said. Israel blew up Gaza's specialised cancer hospital last year after saying troops found a tunnel used by Hamas fighters running beneath it. Asked for comment, COGAT, the Israeli military agency that controls access to Gaza, said it coordinates medical evacuations with the World Health Organisation.

items.title: If you have type O or AB blood, Johor’s Hospital Sultanah Aminah really needs you to come forward this weekend
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 13 — Hospital Sultanah Aminah (HSA) has issued an urgent appeal for type O and AB blood donors as supplies of both types are running low. In a Facebook post, the hospital’s Transfusion Medicine Department said donors can check the Johor Bahru Blood Donation Campaign Schedule page for locations. Blood donation drives are also being held at the Johor Blood Donation Centre at Mid Valley Southkey today through Sunday, from 10am to 6.30pm; AEON Mall Bukit Indah today, Saturday, and Sunday from 10am to 3pm; and at the HSA Blood Donation Centre today and tomorrow from 8am to 4.30pm.

items.title: 6 Paskal personnel rescued after drifting off course in free-fall exercise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Six Royal Malaysian Navy Special Warfare Forces (Paskal) personnel were rescued after drifting from their intended landing position during a free-fall exercise in the South China Sea. The RMN said the personnel were found safe at sea by its vessels. "The incident demonstrated the effectiveness of Paskal's continuous and realistic training in preparing its personnel to deal with unforeseen situations," it said in a Facebook post.

items.title: First AW189 helicopter lands as MMEA steps up patrols, rescues at sea
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Aug 13 — The sovereignty of the country’s 556,285 square kilometres (km) of waters is now strengthened with the receipt of the first of four Medium Lift AW189 helicopters acquired for use by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA). Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the helicopter would enhance the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency’s capabilities in carrying out aerial surveillance, enforcement, search and rescue (SAR) operations, medical evacuation (medevac) and special operations. Also present were Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman and MMEA director-general Admiral Maritime Datuk Rosli Abdullah.

items.title: PublicInvest sees nearly 40pct upside for MSC
items.summary: MSC posted a more than two-fold increase in net profit for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q2 FY26), driven by higher tin prices, stronger sales volumes and improved operational efficiencies. Net profit rose to RM34 million in the quarter from RM13.95 million a year earlier, while revenue jumped 68.2 per cent year-on-year to RM637.3 million. The tin mining segment remained MSC's main earnings contributor, with pre-tax profit rising to RM59.1 million, supported by higher tin production volumes and stronger tin prices.

items.title: Teacher remanded over alleged assault involving student, mother in Kelantan
items.summary: PASIR MAS: A 54-year-old teacher has been remanded for three days to assist investigations into an alleged assault involving a 14-year-old student and his mother. Police arrested the teacher yesterday after receiving a report from the student's mother. Pasir Mas police chief Assistant Commissioner Mazlan Hassan confirmed the report.

items.title: Malaysian police granted access to question pilot detained in Jakarta over drug case, says home minister
items.summary: SUBANG, Aug 13 — Indonesian authorities have reportedly allowed Malaysian police investigators to question a Malaysian pilot detained on suspicion of drug trafficking after he allegedly flew from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to Jakarta with drugs in his luggage. According to the New Straits Times, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said a Narcotics Crime Investigation Department team sent to Jakarta had been granted access to interview the suspect. The 39-year-old pilot was detained at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on July 28 after Indonesian authorities allegedly found 70,114 ecstasy pills and four grammes of methamphetamine in his luggage.

items.title: MSA Media Festival and Awards 2026 brings industry leaders together
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Media Specialists Association (MSA) will host its 2026 Festival and Awards on Aug 14, bringing together media practitioners and industry leaders to discuss the future of Malaysia's media landscape. 355 ENTRIES RECEIVED A total of 126 finalists progressed to the second round of judging on July 14, where they were assessed by more than 65 industry experts, including senior clients, agency practitioners and industry veterans. They include TV Sarawak, Google, Nexxen, OMNiA, Astro, Affinity, Adzymic, Teads, Seni Jaya, WOW Media, BorgRise SVL, Target Media and Silverpush.

items.title: Johor to install 5,000 smart CCTVs across Greater JB to boost security
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Johor government will install about 5,000 smart closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras across Greater JB over the next five years to boost state security. State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the installation of additional smart CCTVs forms part of state efforts to enhance safety. He said the target covers local authorities under the Greater JB region, comprising the Johor Baru City Council (MBJB), Pasir Gudang City Council (MBPG), Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP), and Kulai Municipal Council (MPKu).

items.title: Fresh fruit, veg and protein could soon be added to SARA aid, says Zahid
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 13 — Today’s 18th Executive Committee meeting of the National Cost of Living Action Council (NACCOL) conducted an in-depth review of the local white rice roadmap, which includes a transitional framework to cushion the impact on vulnerable groups. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who chaired the meeting, said tackling the cost of living must go beyond supermarket shelf prices to address production costs, supply chains, access to nutritious food, healthcare and education costs, and support for vulnerable groups. The government is taking cost pressures on business, logistics, and agriculture seriously, he said, including the impact of geopolitical developments, uncertainty in West Asia, import compliance costs, and subsidy rationalisation on food production expenses.

items.title: Romania begins shutdown of nuclear plant due to low Danube
items.summary: BUCHAREST: Romania began Thursday the complete shutdown of its only nuclear plant after water levels in the Danube, used to cool the site, fell to a record low, the national nuclear energy company said. Nuclearelectrica already shut down last month one of the two reactors at the Cernavoda power plant, which usually generates a fifth of the Eastern European country's total electricity. Romania has been trying for days to avert a complete shutdown of the plant's two 700MW reactors.

items.title: Johor to emulate Netherlands model in managing strays
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Johor will emulate the Netherlands' approach to manage stray dogs and cats more effectively, safely, and humanely through collaboration with non-governmental organisations (NGOs). State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the state government would partner with NGOs to address the issue. Currently, only the Johor Bahru City Council (MBJB) operates a shelter housing stray dogs in the district.

items.title: Commuter rescued after falling onto Gombak LRT tracks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A commuter fainted and fell onto the tracks at Gombak LRT station this morning and was rescued by Rapid KL personnel and auxiliary police. Rapid KL said operations personnel and auxiliary police responded immediately to carry out the rescue. Rapid KL said train operations resumed at 9.12am after safety checks confirmed the tracks were clear and safe.

items.title: [UPDATED] Passport forgery syndicate busted, RM200,000 found in e-wallet linked to mastermind
items.summary: Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said two Bangladeshi men, aged 29 and 32, were arrested during raids at two condominium units in Taman Wahyu, Kampung Batu, Kuala Lumpur, about 11.30am yesterday. Zakaria said the suspected mastermind had been in Malaysia for about nine years. Authorities seized two genuine Bangladeshi passports, nine suspected forged Bangladeshi passports, three mobile phones, 700 passport pages and 300 passport covers for various countries believed to be fake.

items.title: [UPDATED] Immigration officers find fake registered addresses in fraudulent PLKS probe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Immigration officers attempting to track down holders of fraudulently issued Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) have hit a snag after finding that registered addresses are also fake. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department conducted several raids at addresses linked to the affected permits as part of ongoing investigations. Zakaria said the department would continue tracing the affected PLKS holders.

items.title: [UPDATED] Two airlines face issues processing Malaysian passports valid beyond 10 years, says Immigration DG
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Only two airlines have encountered problems processing Malaysian passports with validity exceeding 10 years, says Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban. He said the issue was confined to the systems used by the two airlines and did not involve foreign immigration authorities rejecting Malaysian passports. Zakaria said Malaysian passports issued with validity of up to 10 years and six months were valid and recognised in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) standards.

items.title: Putin visit to disputed islands 'unacceptable': Japan PM
items.summary: TOKYO: Russian President Vladimir Putin's visit on Thursday to the Kuril islands is "unacceptable", Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said, with Tokyo also claiming the territory. "This visit... by the sitting Russian president goes against Japan's consistent position on the Northern Territories," Takaichi told reporters, using the Japanese name for the islands, saying Putin's trip "offends the sentiments of the Japanese people and is absolutely unacceptable." Putin on Wednesday called Japan's sanctions "unprovoked".

items.title: 6 teenagers arrested over armed attack in Kuantan
items.summary: KUANTAN: Six teenagers have been arrested following an armed attack at a business premises in Jalan Air Putih here that left two people seriously injured. Kuantan police chief Assistant Commissioner Ashari Abu Samah said the victims lodged a police report claiming they were attacked by a group of men at about 2am on Monday. Ashari said police, acting on information, arrested a suspect in Alor Akar at about 2pm the following day, before arresting another five teenagers near a basketball court in Bukit Setongkol several hours later.

items.title: Rehda Institute: One-size-fits-all RM300,000 housing cap needs rethink
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Rehda Institute views positively the government’s indication that affordable housing may move away from the uniform RM300,000 price ceiling towards a more income-based model, saying affordability benchmarks should reflect local household incomes and actual demand. “Furthermore, housing prices must also recognise actual delivery costs,” it said in a statement following the government’s decision to draft and amend four housing laws under the National Housing Policy (NHP) 2026-2035. Rehda Institute said better use of data on household formation, income, demographics, housing stock, vacancy rates, unsold completed units and mobility patterns could help address persistent supply-demand mismatches, unsold housing and abandoned developments.

items.title: Bandar Utama murder trial: Teen in dock says sorry in court over schoolmate’s death
items.summary: Earlier, Foong informed the court that the defence would rely on the expert testimony of a psychiatrist to support a claim of unsoundness of mind under Section 84 of the Penal Code. Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony, from Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, was called as an expert witness under Section 45 of the Evidence Act 1950, to testify on the teenager’s mental state, including the referral process, treatment and clinical findings. Foong added that the expert believed a long treatment gap could worsen mental illness, especially when it begins in childhood.

items.title: Fadhlina urges calm over pupil protection policy concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek has called on educators to remain calm and give the Education Ministry room to explain the School Pupil Protection Policy following concerns raised by various parties. She said the policy was designed to ensure comprehensive protection for all parties dealing with pupils, prioritising the safety of students, teachers, and the wider school community. The policy, announced via a Professional Circular (SPI) dated July 1, requires staff and external parties with official dealings with schools to sign a School Pupil Protection Policy Compliance Pledge as proof of their commitment to pupil safety.

items.title: Pride in the passport: Reflection ahead of Merdeka
items.summary: When she raised an eyebrow, I clarified, "Malaysia." Your country's passport is strong too." My little red passport.

items.title: Two weeks of beatings, 29 injuries: Top court upholds death sentence for man who killed four-year-old stepson in Klang
items.summary: A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang, Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and Datuk Mohd Nazlan Mohd Ghazali dismissed Mohd Sazly Zamry’s final appeal against his conviction and sentence. Justice Rhodzariah said the death sentence was the only punishment commensurate with the crime committed by Mohd Sazly, 49. Justice Rhodzariah said Mohd Sazly was the sole custodian of the deceased for two weeks at the material time, while his wife was at work.

items.title: Berita Harian's Didik gives teachers, pupils added learning resource
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The revival of Berita Harian's (BH) educational pullout, Didik, provides teachers and pupils with valuable supplementary material that connects classroom learning with real-world contexts, says the Negri Sembilan Education Department. Its Preschool and Primary Unit senior assistant director Halida Yunus said the Special Year 4 Learning Matrix Edition would help foster reading interest, comprehension, critical thinking and awareness of real-world issues among pupils. The Year 4 Learning Matrix offers an engaging way to incorporate newspaper content into pupils' learning experiences," she said at the handover of Didik newspapers at SK Seremban 2B here today.

items.title: Teacher remanded over alleged assault involving student, mother in Kelantan
items.summary: PASIR MAS: A 54-year-old teacher has been remanded for three days to assist investigations into an alleged assault involving a 14-year-old student and his mother. Police arrested the teacher yesterday after receiving a report from the student's mother. Pasir Mas police chief Assistant Commissioner Mazlan Hassan confirmed the report.

items.title: After calling in 115 witnesses and detaining seven suspects, MACC now weighs foreign forensic help to untangle Tabung Haji probe
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is considering engaging foreign forensic experts to assist in its investigation into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the investigation involves matters relating to investments, agreements and contracts, and therefore requires detailed forensic examination. He said the examination would also cover meeting minutes and various documents relating to investment decisions.

items.title: Federal Court upholds death sentence of former chef for murdering stepson
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court today upheld the death sentence imposed on a former chef for the murder of his four-year-old stepson in 2015. A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang, Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali, and Datuk Mohd Nazlan Mohd Ghazali dismissed Mohd Sazly Zamry's final appeal against his conviction and sentence. She said the death sentence was the only punishment commensurate with the crime committed by Sazly, 49.

items.title: Hoping for a downpour to wash away the smog? MetMalaysia says it won’t be enough for the next five days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — The haze situation currently affecting the country is not expected to show any significant changes for the next three to five days, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). MetMalaysia National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre (POCGN) senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said that although rain is forecast to occur in several places, it is not yet able to restore air quality on a large scale. “We hope the rain will help, but if the air is very hazy, a little rain may not be able to remove the effects of the haze,” he said when interviewed on Bernama TV’s ‘Focus 15: Cross-Border Haze Threat.’

items.title: Lorry driver fined RM9,000 over eight-vehicle crash in Batu Pahat
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A lorry driver was fined RM9,000 by the magistrate's court here today after pleading guilty to careless driving that caused an eight-vehicle pile-up early this month. The court also ordered the accused to serve six months' imprisonment if he failed to pay the fine, which he subsequently paid. Investigations concluded that the accused drove without due care and attention for other road users.

items.title: Lawyers group urges MBS to scrap cash for capture dog programme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A lawyers' group has urged the Seremban City Council (MBS) to scrap its "cash-for-capture" dog programme, saying it encourages pet theft and exposes the public to unnecessary risks. Lawyers for Animal Rights (LAR) said MBS's "Program Pemberian Insentif Penyerahan Anjing Terbiar Secara Sukarela 2026" offers RM50 for each adult dog and RM25 for each puppy handed over. The group said the Veterinary Services Department (DVS) classifies dog catching as hazardous work requiring trained personnel, yet MBS was offering incentives to members of the public to capture stray dogs.

items.title: Rocky's death: Man says viral video sparked threats, backlash
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A 24-year-old man facing intense online backlash and death threats over the death of a dog named Rocky has denied abusing or killing the animal. Muhammad Shah Hizam said he was distressed by accusations following a viral video alleging he tortured and killed the dog during an operation at Taman Telok Gedong Indah in Klang on July 29. "I live under extreme pressure, receiving intense criticism and death threats after Rocky's death," he told a #Justiceforshah press conference in Bukit Jelutong here today.

items.title: Prima facie proven: Court says Bandar Utama boy must enter defence in schoolmate’s murder
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 13 — The High Court today ordered a 15-year-old boy to enter his defence on a charge of murdering a female student at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year. Judge Adlin Abdul Majid issued the order after finding that the prosecution had successfully established a prima facie case against the teenager. Lawyer Kitson Foong, representing the accused, confirmed the court order to reporters after this morning’s proceedings.

items.title: Johor to add 5,000 smart CCTVs across Greater Johor Bahru in five years
items.summary: PASIR GUDANG, Aug 13 – The Johor government plans to install 5,000 more smart closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras across Greater Johor Bahru over the next five years to improve public safety, said State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor. The cameras will be installed across four local authority areas as part of Johor’s push to become a Smart State through greater use of technology. “We are targeting about 5,000 new smart CCTV cameras next year in the Greater JB region, that includes local authorities from the Johor Bahru City Council (MBJB), Pasir Gudang City Council, Iskandar Puteri City Council and Kulai Municipal Council.

items.title: Tabung Haji reforms must go beyond RCI findings, says BN sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Barisan Nasional (BN) wants all recommendations in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the management and operations of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2014 to 2020 to be fully implemented to strengthen confidence among its 10 million depositors. BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the measures were also necessary to further strengthen TH governance. “BN believes the special parliamentary sitting provided ample room for public scrutiny of the TH RCI report.

items.title: Johor wants to give stray dogs a better shot at life, Netherlands-style
items.summary: PASIR GUDANG, Aug 13 — The Johor government plans to adopt the Netherlands’ widely cited approach to managing stray animals, including sterilisation, shelter care and adoption. State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the state government would work with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to address the stray dog and cat population. Mohd Jafni said the stray dogs would be neutered and properly cared for before being offered for adoption.

items.title: Someone left two suitcases at KLIA’s Lost and Found, Customs found RM3.8m in cannabis — and more hidden in toy boxes
items.summary: SEPANG, Aug 13 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Customs foiled four smuggling cases last month, seizing 1.53 million cigarette sticks and 60.47 kg of cannabis buds worth more than RM6.17 million, including duties and taxes. Its director Aspalila Ag Tuah said two of the cases involved cigarette smuggling at the KLIA Free Commercial Zone, while the other two involved cannabis buds, including 47.8 kg of the drug worth RM3.824 million that was found in two pieces of luggage abandoned at the Lost and Found office in the International Arrival Hall of KLIA Terminal 1. Aspalila said in another drug case on July 13, the department seized 12.675 kg of cannabis buds worth RM1.014 million that had been concealed in children’s toy boxes.

items.title: Fadhlina urges calm, says ministry needs space to explain school pupil protection pledge policy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek called on educators to remain calm and give the Ministry of Education (MOE) room to explain the School Pupil Protection Policy, which has recently caused concern among many parties. She said the policy was designed to ensure comprehensive protection for all parties dealing with pupils, with priority given to the safety of students, teachers and the entire school community. The SPI outlines five main areas of education reform, namely mental health; reproductive and social health education; child sexual violence and substance abuse prevention; pupil protection policy; teacher welfare; and pupil voice.

items.title: Transport Ministry to refer commingled oil tax issue to MOF for clarification
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — The Transport Ministry will seek clarification from the Finance Ministry over concerns surrounding the tax treatment of commingled oil cargo, Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said today. Loke said his ministry had yet to be informed of any new taxation involving such cargo, adding that the matter falls under the purview of the Royal Malaysian Customs Department and the Finance Ministry. Loke was responding to concerns raised by maritime industry players over uncertainty surrounding the tax treatment of commingled oil cargo at Malaysian ports.

items.title: Penang’s new air logistics complex set to boost northern cargo capacity, says Anthony Loke
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 13 — The Penang International Logistics Aeropark (Pila) is set to significantly boost air cargo facilities and capacity in Malaysia’s northern region, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke. He said the project, an expansion of the existing Penang air cargo hub, would provide much greater capacity and strengthen the region’s role as an air logistics centre. It is next to the current Penang cargo hub,” he said.

items.title: DAP northern delegates gather to discuss party’s future ahead of Aug 16 national congress
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 13 — About 400 DAP delegates from Penang, Kedah and Perlis attended an engagement session with party secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook and the Central Executive Committee (CEC) leadership here last night. The session, held ahead of the party’s national congress on Aug 16, served as a platform for delegates to exchange views on party affairs, national issues and the party’s future direction. The upcoming congress is expected to see delegates deliberate on the party’s position and future direction within the Unity Government.

items.title: Perak police probe sexual harassment allegations against PKNPk CEO
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 13 — Perak police have opened an investigation into alleged slander involving sexual harassment claims against Perak State Development Corporation (PKNPk) chief executive officer Datuk Redza Rafiq Abdul Razak, following a report lodged by the corporation. State police chief commissioner Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the investigation was initiated based on the police report lodged by PKNPk over the matter, which had been circulated on social media. Mohd Alwi said police had yet to receive any report from the alleged sexual harassment victim.

items.title: Alam Flora regrets impact, pledges safety focus as Pantai Hillpark lorry crash probe continues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Alam Flora has pledged its full cooperation with authorities in the probe into a crash involving one of its compactor garbage lorries along Jalan Pantai Murni 1, Pantai Hillpark, yesterday. In a statement today, Alam Flora informed that the vehicle will be sent for inspection to identify the exact cause of the incident, in line with instructions from the investigating officer. “We deeply regret the impact this incident has had on the affected community and remain committed to ensuring high safety standards in all our operational activities,” the statement read.

items.title: Meth, heroin and cannabis worth RM18,500 found inside a Lumut police cell, and a cop's in trouble too
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 13 — Three men, including a police constable, were arrested after police seized drugs worth RM18,534 at the Lumut police station lock-up in Manjung. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the drugs were found during an inspection of the lock-up on Tuesday at about 8.30am. He said police found 16 small plastic tubes containing 109g of methamphetamine, 16 plastic tubes containing 110g of heroin and 23 tubes containing 142g of dried cannabis leaves.

items.title: Jobstreet: Firms still keen on hiring, job ads grew 33pc year-on-year
items.summary: “Jobstreet’s platform data reflects continued hiring demand. In H1 2026, job ads increased by 33 per cent year-on-year, showing that employers are still actively looking for talent across the market,” said Nicholas Lam, managing director, Jobstreet by SEEK Malaysia. Manufacturing, transport and logistics accounted for the largest share of job ads at 12 per cent, followed by accounting at 11 per cent, sales at 10 per cent, engineering at 9 per cent, and administration and office support at 8 per cent, the platform said citing its internal data.

items.title: ‘I am very relaxed’: Loke dismisses talk of final ministry assembly before DAP congress decision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today played down suggestions that this could be his last monthly assembly with Transport Ministry staff ahead of DAP’s crucial vote on Sunday on whether the party should remain in the federal government. Asked whether today’s ministry assembly could be his final one with ministry staff, Loke dismissed the assumption. Asked if he was nervous ahead of the DAP special congress on Sunday, Loke said he was relaxed.

items.title: Transport minister urges commercial vehicle drivers to make RM30 health screening count as fewer than 20 sign up
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Fewer than 20 commercial vehicle drivers have taken up the government’s subsidised health screening programme since it was launched last month, Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said today. Loke said the programme was aimed at improving the health and wellbeing of drivers, particularly those responsible for carrying passengers and operating commercial vehicles. Loke urged drivers, particularly older ones, to undergo comprehensive health screenings to identify potential health problems early.
